This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: attempt ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 questions answered. Section B: answer BOTH questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Classify the following substances into acids and Bases: Vinegar, Soapy water, Lemon juice, Bitter leaf juice.

| Acid | Base |
|---|---|
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  |  | *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Acid | Base |
|---|---|
| Vinegar | Soapy water |
| Lemon juice | Bitter leaf juice |

Vinegar (ethanoic acid) and lemon juice (citric acid) taste sour: they are acids. Soapy water and bitter leaf juice are bitter or soapy to the touch: they are bases (alkaline).

questions.enonce_markdown: State two physical properties of acids. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Acids have a **sour taste** (for example lemon juice; dilute acids only, never taste laboratory acids).
2. Their aqueous solutions **conduct electricity** (they are electrolytes).

(Other acceptable answers: they are soluble in water, and many are colourless liquids or solutions.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
State the effect of lemon juice and soapy water on red Litmus paper.

Lemon juice: ...

Soapy water: ... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- **Lemon juice:** red litmus paper stays **red** (no change), because lemon juice is acidic; acids turn blue litmus red.
- **Soapy water:** red litmus paper turns **blue**, because soapy water is alkaline.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Sodium hydroxide reacts with sulphuric acid to form a salt and water only.

(i) Name the reaction type.

(ii) Identify the salt formed.

(iii) Write an equation for the reaction.

(iv) State how the salt crystals can be obtained from the salt solution. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Neutralisation** (an acid reacts with a base to form a salt and water only).

(ii) The salt is **sodium sulphate**, $\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}$.

(iii) $2\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \rightarrow \mathrm{Na_2SO_4} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$

(Balance check: Na 2 = 2, S 1 = 1, H 2 + 2 = 4 = 4, O 2 + 4 = 6 = 4 + 2.)

(iv) **Heat the solution gently to evaporate some of the water** until it is saturated (a drop on a cold glass rod forms crystals), then **leave it to cool and crystallise**; filter off the crystals, wash them with a little cold distilled water and dry them between filter papers.
